evidence.field: Character evolution page; graph interpretation and script categories
evidence.text: The entry identifies 日 as resembling the sun and says its original meaning is the sun. It lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen categories, including bronze inscription 集成05990. Its text supports the broad script categories but does not date each displayed form.
evidence.title: 漢字「日」：字形演變

evidence.field: 形義通解; oracle-bone glyph and cited inscriptional uses
evidence.text: The entry describes 日 as a sun image, says the original form was round and some forms became square because circles were difficult to carve on oracle bones, and says the central mark distinguished 日 from 囗. It cites Shang oracle-bone examples for the sun and sunrise (合集34163), eclipse (合集11480), daylight opposed to evening (合集33871, 合集34036), a five-day period (合集12314), and a sacrificial name (合集27463). These citations attest distinct uses but do not establish their order or all semantic links.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：日

evidence.field: 形義通解; bronze inscriptions and received Shuowen analysis
evidence.text: The entry reports bronze-inscription use for the sun, daylight contrasted with night, and calendar-day expressions including 今日 and 翌日. It also cites 日 before calendrical names in an ancestor designation and reports Tang Lan's interpretation as a ritual-day ranking. For the received Shuowen entry, CUHK gives 从囗、一 and notes that glossing 日 by 實 is a Han-era phonetic explanation, not necessarily the graph's original construction.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：日

evidence.text: The character-specific page labels record 27.65E5 as a small-seal form under 說文‧日部 and displays 日 as the regular-script form. It verifies this labeled seal-script candidate's character association; the page does not provide an ancient artifact image or an individual archaeological date.
evidence.title: 小學堂字形

evidence.field: File description, source attribution, reuse rights, and file history
evidence.text: The exact page describes 日-seal.svg as a vector depiction of 日 in Shuowen seal-script style, identifies Xiaoxuetang image 27.65E5 as a source, and links to a CC0 notice for the Xiaoxuetang glyph image and to a CC0 dedication for this SVG. It is a modern digital drawing: file history records uploads beginning 10 July 2006. The page also lists Shang oracle and bronze versions as other versions; those links indicate candidates exist, but were not inspected here. The embedded image itself was not visually inspected in this run, so identity and style rely on the file page's description and Xiaoxuetang label.
evidence.title: File:日-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: Official reuse notice for query-interface glyph images and glyph-attribute information
evidence.text: The notice explicitly places glyph images and glyph-attribute information obtained through the site's query interface under CC0 1.0. This notice does not grant permission to reproduce the site's linked dictionary text wholesale.
evidence.title: 版權聲明 - 小學堂文字學資料庫

search_audit.outcome: The Shuowen.org page opened without readable text in the tool. CUHK's character page supplied the received Shuowen quotation and commentary on its interpretation.
The exact candidate page was attempted but inaccessible; its local metadata lead was not counted as verified evidence.
Search surfaced third-party mirrors, but the official Unicode character lookup was attempted and inaccessible. No mirror was used as substitute for the required official character record.

gaps: The CUHK entry cites Shang oracle-bone catalogue numbers but this research did not independently verify dates for each individual inscription; treat them as Shang-period examples, not securely dated first attestations.

The evidence attests sun, daylight, day-unit, and sacrificial-name uses in oracle-bone contexts but does not establish their relative chronology or all semantic transitions. Later Chinese and Japanese sense histories were not researched beyond the cited inscriptional and dictionary data.
Early forms are interpreted as a sun depiction. The received Shuowen segmentation 从囗一 does not independently establish that the graph originally consisted of those components.

The seal candidate has verified descriptive provenance and license but no visual inspection of its pixels. The alternative exact Commons candidate page was inaccessible. No image is selected on this evidence.
The official Unihan record could not be opened; kMandarin rì remains supported only by the supplied local row and was not emitted as externally verified evidence.

No component sound analysis applies: 日 is treated here as a whole-graph sun pictogram. Dossier statements about loans or 金 assimilation were not established as explanations of this graph's sun/day history.
